newsitem.title: USA: NY official sees few public funds for Yankees stay.
newsitem.headline: NY official sees few public funds for Yankees stay.

text.p: The chairman of Empire State Development Corp, who is participating in talks to help keep the Yankees American League baseball team in New York City, said Wednesday the state could not absorb most of the cost of a renovated or new stadium.
Though noting the Pataki Administration does not want the team to move, Charles Gargano said, "However, one thing we cannot do is commit large taxpayer dollars to what is a private enterprise."
New York State plans to soon contract Morgan Stanley & Co to study whether the Yankee Stadium in the Bronx should be refurbished or a new one built on the west side of Manhattan around 34th Street.

Gargano, who spoke at a breakfast sponsored by Crain's New York Business, raised the possibility of creating a new sports financing authority to help professional sports teams in the state, including the Yankees as well as the Mets National League baseball team and the Buffalo Bills football team.

He explained such an authority might use a variety of funding methods to help the teams meet their capital needs. He said the methods might include selling debt or the name of a stadium, as well as licensing fees.
The state official added he had yet to discuss the idea of a new sports authority with Gov George Pataki and had no immediate plans to submit a bill to the Legislature to create such an agency.
